overall: The AG found the Board violated the OML by meeting December 27 without 48-hour notice (no emergency) and by failing to accommodate overflow at the December 29 Zoom meeting; no violation on remote-member announcements; public-comment claim declined.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly met December 27 on a mask mandate without posting notice 48 hours in advance, claiming an emergency.
allegations.key_passage: For these reasons, we find that the circumstances surrounding the December 27 meeting did not meet the criteria for an emergency meeting under the Open Meeting Law and, therefore, the Board violated the Law by failing to post notice of the meeting 48 hours in advance.

allegations.summary: December 29 remote meeting allegedly not open to all who tried to attend, since the Zoom account capped participants at 300 and people were turned away.
allegations.key_passage: For a meeting that was foreseeably crowded, the Board did not make reasonable efforts to accommodate the overflow crowd.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly failed to announce which members would participate remotely at the December 29 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that it was evident to the public which Board members were participating remotely, thus fulfilling the transparency goals of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly stopped accepting public comment after 30 minutes at the December 29 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: even if true, this allegation would not constitute a violation of G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25 as the Open Meeting Law does not guarantee a right to public participation in public body meetings.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
All Board members attend an Open Meeting Law webinar training provided by the AG's office within 90 days of receipt of the letter
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Board that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
